bibl.title: Female Agency by the Dead Sea: Evidence from the Babatha and Salome Komaïse Archives.
bibl.seg: Philip F. Esler, Female Agency by the Dead Sea: Evidence from the Babatha and Salome Komaïse Archives.
bibl.note: 1. Framing the discussion: 1.1. The recent scholarly assertion of female agency in the biblical world; - 1.2. The Babatha and Salome Komaïse archives; - 1.3. The disclosure of social worlds in legal documents. - 2. The basis of female agency: women as possessors of capital: 2.1. The unusual agricultural context; - 2.2. The role of dowries in context; - 2.3. Limitations to the benefits of dowries for women; - 2.4. The value of dowries; - 2.5. Women as owners of date-palm plantation; - 2.6. Were the women of Maoza atypically wealthy? - 3. Female agency in business: 3.1. ’Amat-’Isi: a Nabatean businesswoman; - 3.2. Babatha's loans to her second husband; - 3.3. ’Abi-‘adan's loan to her husband; - 3.4. Conclusion. - 4. Female agency in litigation: 4.1 Babatha's litigation against her son's legal guardians; - 4.2. Babatha's seizure of her second husband's date-plantations; - 4.3. The litigation between Babatha and her late husband's other wife; - 4.4. Conclusion. - 5. Women and their guardians: 5.1. Women’s guardianship pursuant to Roman law in the province of Arabia; - 5.2. The limits on women's guardianship. - 6. Conclusion.
